title: Neural networks, without the mystery
learning_objective: Explain how inputs become a prediction through weighted connections and repeated layers.

scenes.title: Start with inputs
scenes.summary: A model receives measurable signals represented as numbers.
scenes.narration: We begin with numbers that describe the thing we want the model to reason about.
scenes.fallback: Inputs are numeric measurements such as pixel brightness or sensor readings.

scenes.title: Connections change influence
scenes.summary: Each incoming value is multiplied by a weight before signals are combined.
scenes.fallback: Input values are scaled by weights, added together, transformed, then passed forward.

scenes.title: Many simple units form a network
scenes.summary: A layer transforms one vector of numbers into another.
scenes.fallback: Three input nodes connect to four hidden nodes, which connect to two output nodes.

scenes.title: Training changes the weights
scenes.summary: The model compares predictions with targets and adjusts weights to reduce error.
scenes.fallback: Training repeatedly changes weights so predictions better match targets.

scenes.title: Error falls across repeated updates
scenes.summary: A training curve shows the direction of learning without turning the page into a dashboard.
scenes.fallback: Loss decreases from 62 to 23 over six training steps.

scenes.title: Representations occupy a space
scenes.summary: A restrained spatial view can clarify relative position when depth carries meaning.
scenes.fallback: Eight muted points are arranged in a shallow arc to suggest an abstract representation space; the exact geometry is illustrative, not measured data.
